videos.title: Cristóbal de Morales: Salva nos, stella maris (c.1535)

localized.title: Cristóbal de Morales: Salva nos, stella maris (c.1535)
localized.description:
Salva nos, stella maris

  0:00  Original motet (SAATB)
  1:35  Arrangement for pipe organ

Cristóbal de Morales, spent much of his career traversing between Toledo and Rome. He was a composer, chorister, music director and organist in Toledo (perhaps at the main cathedral) and is regarded as the earliest of the Spanish composers who developed an international reputation. This very short work appears in a Toledo collection from around 1545. It is a devotional piece to the Virgin Mary that was likely intended for the post-Christmas period — specifically the Feast of the Epiphany (or Festival of the Three Kings).

I used the MAIKA Spanish language Vocaloid to generate the sound of the SAATB choir. The pipe organ sound was created using the iPhone app Music Studio 2. 

Text:

Salva nos, stella maris
Tu quae tenes in gremio Regem
cui reges coeunt
aurum, thus, myrrham offerunt

Translation:

Save us, star of the sea,
you who hold in [your] lap the King,
to whom kings gather:
they offer gold, frankincense, and myrrh

Description of the photos:

1. Adoration of the Magi, Giorgio Vasari, c1566
2. Madonna and Child, Antonio Begarelli, 1540
3. Adoration of the Kings, Giorgione, 1506
4. Pipe organ loft, 16th Century, Chiesa in Santo Spirito in Sassia, Rome -- an instrument probably similar to the one on which de Morales may have performed during his tenure in Rome.
5. Interior of Toledo Cathedral in Spain, where de Morales was maestro de capilla.

videos.title: [New Rendition] P. Attaingnant & C. Geoffray: Tourdion "Magdalena" (1530) & "Quand je bois" (1949)

localized.title: [New Rendition] P. Attaingnant & C. Geoffray: Tourdion "Magdalena" (1530) & "Quand je bois" (1949)
localized.description:
Tourdion "Magdalena" (1530) & "Quand je bois du vin claret" (1949)

  0:06  Tourdion "Magdalena": recorders, lute, dulcimer, bass viol, bass drum, tambourine
  2:07  "Quand je bois du vin claret": ATTB

This popular Tourdion is the lively conclusion to the Basse danse "La Magdalena" from one of Pierre Attaingnant's many meticulously printed volumes of French and Italian courtly dances. The "Quand je bois du vin claret," on the other hand, is a short satirical piece by the 20th Century French composer and choirmaster César Geoffray based on the same Tourdion tune and written in the style of a 16th Century drinking song. The upper voice has a different set of lyrics than the lower voices - as was not uncommon in the late medieval period. The 6/4 rhythm and melody in the lower voices is somewhat similar to the "L"homme arme" tune of the late 15th century. Geoffray's lyrics are adapted from an anonymous chanson published by Scotto in Venice in 1535 -- a song that has an entirely different melody. 

The vocal simulation was created using the Maika Spanish language voice bank and the Vocaloid voice encoder program. Other than for the frontally trilled "r" sound, I used modern French pronunciation to respect the song's 20th Century origins. In this latest rendition, I created a more legato effect, added slight dynamic variation and corrected some vowel sounds. The instrumental sounds were produced using the iPhone app Music Studio 2.

Text:

Quand je bois du vin clairet, (When I drink the Bordeaux red)
Ami tout tourne, tourne, tourne, tourne... (my friend, everything turns, turns...)
Aussi désormais je bois (Now I also drink)
Anjou ou Arbois. (Anjou or Arbois wines)

Chantons et buvons: (We sing and drink)
À ce flacon faisons la guerre! (We declare war on this flask of wine)
Chantons et buvons (We sing and drink)
Mes amis; buvons donc! (My friends, then we drink)

4. Wedding dance, Pieter Brueghel the Elder, 1566
5. Temperate and Intemperate, Anon. Flemish, c1480
6. Grapes on the vine in the area of Lyon, the locale where César Geoffray was music director at the time of this composition.

videos.title: [New Rendition] Gilles de Binchois or Walter Frye: Tout a par moy (c.1450)

localized.title: [New Rendition] Gilles de Binchois or Walter Frye: Tout a par moy (c.1450)
localized.description:
Tout a par moy a 3

  0:06  Verse 1 (SAT)
  1:57  Verse 2 (SAT + lute, psaltery, harp)

The French rondeau "Tout a par moy" has two attributions, both highly esteemed composers at the sumptuous court of Burgundy in the mid-15 Century: the Netherlander Gilles Binchois (a.k.a. Gilles de Binche) and the Englishman Walter Frye.  The tune was undoubtedly a very popular song as there are many surviving copies and parodies dispersed across northern France and Belgium in luxuriously illuminated manuscripts.  It is a typical 15th Century song of courtly, unrequited love. The lyrics in this variation is taken from the Laborde Chansonnier and is different from other contemporary sources in that the lyrics point to a female protagonist seeking a male lover.

The voices were entered using Vocaloid 4 with MAIKA (a Spanish language voice bank). Reverb and echo effects were added with Audacity. The instrumental doubling was achieved using the iPhone app Music Studio 2. In this latest rendition, I corrected some of the text and the text underlay. I also sped up the tempo significantly, changed the cantus part to a female voice, created a more legato effect, added some natural dynamics and doubled the voices with instruments in Verse 2.

Text:

Verse 1: Tout a par moy, affin qu’on ne me voye,
  si tresdolente que plus je ne pourroye,
  je me tiens seulle comme esbahye
  faisant regretz de ma dolente vie
  et de Fortune qu’ainsi fort me guerroye.

Verse 2: Car j'ay perdu a si que tant chier avoye,
  dont ne m'actens que pur nesune voye
  jamais de rien me trouver resjouye,
  mais languir jusque tant que desvye
  mon deul tenant sans avoir bien ne joye.

Translation:

Verse 1: All by myself, for there is no one who sees me,
  so full of pain that I could not be much sadder,
  I stay by myself like a troubled soul,
  regretting for my sad life
  and Fortune, who so strongly battles me.

Verse 2: Because I have lost that which is most cherished
  whom I expect to never see [again]
  never from nothing will find me rejoicing
  but to languish much until [the end] of life
  my pain remains without there being any good or joy.

1. "Tout a par moy" first page, upper voices, Chansonnier Cordiforme, Paris 2973, c1470. Note that the pages of the book is cut into a heart shape. No attribution.
2. You or Death, detail from a ceremonial shield, French, c1480
3. "Tout a par moy" Laborde Chansonnier, attrib. "Frye" (likely Walter Frye), c1470. 
4. A noble lady, Anonymous French, c1470
5. "Tout a par moy" Mellon Chansonnier (Yale University), attrib. also "Frye," c1470
6. Roman de la Rose, detail of a gallant lost in amorous fantasy, Guillaume de Lorris, Harley MS 4425, c1480
7. "Tout a par moy" 2nd page, lower voices, Chansonnier Cordiforme, Paris 2973, c1470

videos.title: Leonhard Päminger: Resonet in laudibus / In dulci jubilo / Omnis mundus (c.1550)

localized.title: Leonhard Päminger: Resonet in laudibus / In dulci jubilo / Omnis mundus (c.1550)
localized.description:
Resonet in laudibus / In dulci jubilo / Omnis mundus jocundetur

   0:06  Original Lied for 5 voices (SSATB)
   2:18  Instrumental arrangement (shawm, cornetto, 3 trombones, church organ)

This motet for 5 voices can be described as both combinative (polytextual with multiple sets of lyrics sung simultaneously) and macaronic (polylingual with both German and Latin words). All three sets of lyrics, "Resonet in laudibus," "In dulci jubilo" and "Omnis mundus jocundetur" were traditional German Christmas songs from pre-Reformation times. "Resonet" and "In dulci" were each at least 2 centuries old by the time of Päminger's production.

Almost nothing is known about the life of Leonhard Päminger (a.k.a. Paminger in some part books). Nevertheless, he was one of the most prolific composers of the 16th Century with more than 700 attributions -- mostly religious in nature. He was Austrian and Catholic by birth but openly followed the teachings of Martin Luther and maintained a close association with the early Protestant leaders throughout most of his career.

Text (and translation):

Cantus 1:
  Resonet in laudibus (Resonate in praises)
  cum jucundis plausibus (with joyous plaudits)
  Sion cum fidelibus: (to Zion with the faithful)
  apparuit quem genuit Maria (appears the one born of Maria)

Cantus 2:
  In dulci jubilo, (In sweet joy)
  Nun singet und seid froh! (Now sing and be happy)
  Unsers Herzens Wonne liegt (Our hearts lies)
  in praesepio, (in the manger)
  Und leuchtet als die Sonne (and shines as the Sun) 
  Matris in gremio, (in the lap of the mother)
  Alpha es et O! (You are Alpha and Omega!)

Alto, Tenor and Bass:
  Omnis mundus jocundetur nato salvatore
     (The whole word rejoices the Savior's birth)
  casta mater quae concepit Gabrielis ore.
     (the chaste mother who conceives as Gabriel spoke)
  Sonoris vocibus,sinceris mentibus,
     (with sonorous voices, with sincere minds)
  exsultemus et laetemur hodie.
     (We will exult and rejoice today)
  Itaque, gaudete, gaudeamus itaque.
     (Therefore, rejoice! We rejoice, thus!).

videos.title: [New Rendition] Guillaume de Machaut: Aucune gent / Qui plus aimme / Fiat voluntas (c.1350)

localized.title: [New Rendition] Guillaume de Machaut: Aucune gent / Qui plus aimme / Fiat voluntas (c.1350)
localized.description:
This unusual secular motet by the French composer Guillaume de Machaut was likely written around the time of the Black Plague.  There is no mention of disease nor death in the text. Instead, the melancholic and metaphysical mood is directed towards an unrequited love for an imaginary lady -- perhaps to his beloved patron Bonne of Luxembourg who died of the Pestilence in 1349.

The work was intended for performance by 4 vocalists: the upper two cantus parts with different sets of words and meanings while the two lower parts are not associated with any French poetry but rather the Latin phrase "fiat voluntas tua." ("your will be done.") These 3 words were culled from the "Pater noster" (Our Father) chant, but in this context, is expressing the hopelessness of the protagonist who is pining away for an unattainable woman. The motet contains much of what made Machaut famous: the sudden shift in modes, the occasional half or whole step interval between voices on a leading note of a phrase that creates a jarring dissonance, the hocket (hocquetus) effect between the upper voice parts, the incredible poetic eloquence of his verses and so many other experimental features.  The lower two voices are both intoning long notes in the first two-thirds of the piece and then repeat the same notes at twice the tempo in the last third of the piece.

The "sung" portion of this soundtrack was created using Vocaloid 4 with the MAIKA Spanish language module.  The instrumental sounds (medieval lutes, psaltery and harp) were generated using MusicStudio2, an iPhone app. In this latest rendition, I added the phrase "fiat voluntas tua" to both lower voices (instead of a pedal point in the previous version). I also created a more legato effect and a softer tonal quality. Finally, I corrected some pronunciation and changed the triplum (high alto) to a male voice.

Text:

Triplum (Cantus I):
      Aucune gent m'ont demande que j'ai
      Que je ne chant et que ja n'ai cuer gay,
      Si com je sueil chanter de lie corage
      et je leur di, certes, que ja ne say
      mais j'ai menti, car dedens le cuer ai
      un trop grief dueil qui onques n'assouage.
      ETC.

Motetus (Cantus II):
     Qui plus aimme plus endure
     et plus meinne dure vie,
     Au'Amours qui est sans measure
     Asses plus le contralie
     que li mauvais qui n'a cure
     En mal et en villonnie.
     ETC.

Tenor & Countertenor: 
    Fiat voluntas tua

Translation:

Triplum:
     Some have asked what's going on.
     For I have no joy in my heart and I no longer sing
     As I was wont to sing with a light heart
     And I say to them, certainly, I don't know
     But I have lied, for in my heart I have 
     A great sorrow that never assuages.
     ETC.

Motetus:
     Whoever loves more, suffers more
     and more difficult is his life
     for love, which is beyond measure,
     attacks him more than she
     But devotes himself
     to evil and villany.
     ETC.

Tenor & Countertenor: 
    Your will is done.

1. "Aucune gent," Guillaume de Machaut, manuscript from c1370 commissioned by the composer
2. Bonne of Luxembourg (Machaut' patron) with her husband Jean, c1340.
3. Machaut composing a ballade for a Lady.
4. King David with his musical instruments, most importantly his harp.  Lansdowne MS 1175, c1365
5. Romance of Alexander, Bodleian Libr. MS 264, c.1344
6. Illuminated page from Machaut's collected works, c1370

videos.title: [New Rendition] Francisco Guerrero: Ave Virgo sanctissima (1589)

localized.title: [New Rendition] Francisco Guerrero: Ave Virgo sanctissima (1589)
localized.description:
This motet dedicated to the Virgin Mary was composed late in Guerrero's career after his long sojourn in Rome and in other parts of Italy. One can hear elements of the new style of his generation: a simpler, more straightforward, church polyphony with clearly audible lyrics that was the hallmark of the Italian and Spanish Counter-Reformation. One can also hear the rich harmonies of Palestrina and Victoria from contemporary sources. The major counterpoint occurs as a strict canon between the two cantus parts in the alto range. There is a segment of intense emotional drama in the middle of the piece when the singers take turns repeatedly intoning the word "Salve!" (Greetings!) on long suspended notes and recurrent, passing dissonances.

This soundtrack was generated using the Vocaloid 4 encoding software and the MAIKA Spanish language voice bank. The original MIDI file was compiled by James Gibb and can be found at the website cpdl.org. In this latest rendition, I added some natural dynamic variation, created a more legato effect, corrected some pronunciation, changed earlier ficta errors in the original MIDI, generated a brighter sound in Vocaloid and slowed the tempo a bit.

Text:
Ave virgo sanctissima
Dei mater piisima
Maris stella clarissima
Salve semper gloriosa
Margarita pretiosa
Sicut lilium formosa
Nitens olens velut rosa

Translation:
Hail, most sacred Virgin,
most pious Mother of God,
brightest star of the [celestial] ocean.
Greetings, ever glorious,
precious pearl,
like the comely lily,
aromatic as the rose

videos.title: Johann Sebastian Bach: Terzetto from the Christmas Oratorio (1734)

localized.title: Johann Sebastian Bach: Terzetto from the Christmas Oratorio (1734)
localized.description:
Besides the St. Matthew Passion, the Christmas Oratorio is probably J.S. Bach's most massive and elaborate creation. A complete performance of all the movements would have likely run at least 3 hours, and the virtuosic passages throughout his magnum opus would have tested the limits of even the most skilled musicians and singers of his time. It was likely composed for the Lutheran congregation of St. Thomas Church in Leipzig for the Advent season of 1734. It is, at least in part, a compilation of earlier snippets from his cantatas and other smaller works.

This 51st movement at the end of Part 5 is written for solo violin, 3 vocalists (soprano, alto, bass) and continuo. The alto part is added as a response to the other two excited voices who are looking forward to the coming of the Messiah, but his interjections are abrupt and brief. One might find particularly jarring, the shouts of "Ach, wann?" ("O, when") and the response "Schweigt" ("Silence"). The movement is mostly a trio of violin, cantus (probably a boy soprano) and bassus. 

Text:

Sopran:
Ach! wann wird die Zeit erscheinen? Wann? (O, when will the Time appear? When?)
Jesu, ach! so komm zu mir! (Jesus, Oh, come to me!)
Ach! Wann kommt der Trost der Seinen, wann? (When will his comfort come?)

Alt:
Schweigt, er ist schon wirklich hier (Silence, he is really, already here)

Bass:
Ach! Wann kommt der Trost der Seinen (When will his comfort come?)
Jesu, ach! so komm zu mir! (Jesus, Oh, come to me!)
Ach! Wann wird die Zeit erscheinen, wann? (O, when will the Time appear? When?)

Description of the photos:

1. Terzetto "Ach wann wird die Zeit" from Christmas Oratorio (Weihnachtsoratorium), BWV 248, one of the earliest complete editions, copied by Carl Friedrich Zelter, 1734
2. Interior of Thomaskirche (St. Thomas Church) in Leipzig where J.S. Bach composed and likely conducted the Christmas Oratorio
3. Baroque Orchestra, unknown source, likely c1730
4. Exterior of Thomaskirche, Anon. German, 1735
5. Angel playing violin, source unknown, likely Italian, c1630
6. A Lutheran Bible printed in Leipzig in 1708 that might have been used by J.S. Bach for reference during his tenure at Thomaskirche
7. Leipzig in winter, from Pixabay, Veloismus
8. Another angle of the interior of Thomaskirche

videos.title: 多田武彦 男声合唱曲 道

localized.title: 多田武彦 男声合唱曲 道
localized.description:
草野心平作詩
「グリークラブ・ソングセレクションⅡ」に載っている単曲です。
初演が2017年と多田先生のお亡くなりになった年なので最晩年の一曲です。

今まで歩んできた道を振り返り、反省し、これからは正しく大きな道を歩もうと決意する詩です。多田先生からの最後のエールのようにも思えます。

localized.title: 多田武彦 男声合唱組曲「雨」 全6曲
localized.description:
00:00　表紙
00:05　Ⅰ． 雨の来る前　　　 ～伊藤整：作詩
02:26　Ⅱ． 武蔵野の雨　　　 ～大木敦夫：作詩
04:20　Ⅲ． 雨の日の遊動円木 ～大木敦夫：作詩
06:19　Ⅳ． 雨　雨　　　　　 ～尾形亀之助：作詩
08:24　Ⅴ． 雨の日に見る　　 ～大木敦夫：作詩
10:21　Ⅵ． 雨　　　　　　　 ～八木重吉：作詩

演奏：Vocaloid Quartette
  VY2V3 / YOHIOloid / KAITO_V3_Straight / Gackpoid_V4_Power
  (Solo) Ⅵ: VY2V3

楽譜：
https://www.panamusica.co.jp/ja/product/4205/

改訂版で差し替えられた「Ⅳ．十一月にふる雨」も単独曲でUPしました。お聴きください。
https://youtu.be/3cLHKZEh-i0


以下、全くの個人の感想です。悪しからず。
*-----------
多田武彦最高傑作の組曲の一つで、各曲が珠玉の名作でした。過去形です。
やさしさ・慈愛に満ち溢れた親しみやすい曲の中に異質で高難度な「雨　雨」が入りバランスの悪いものになったと感じます。
削除された「十一月にふる雨」が、「武蔵野の雨」「雨」とともにこの組曲の中の超名曲であり、楽譜が正規ルートで手に入らない現状は残念です。差別用語が完全に歴史上の言葉、死語になり、差別用語で傷つく人がいなくなって、再びこの曲が堂々と歌われるようになってほしい。
あと、「雨の来る前」が他の曲と比べると曲想転換が多く凝った作品のように感じます。コンクール課題曲になったと聞くと納得しますが、それ以外の曲の方が旋律が美しく肩の力が抜けたシンプルさを感じます。芸術性を追求して書かれた曲でない方が名曲になるのかもしれないと邪推します。
ボカロに歌ってもらう際、実は「雨　雨」に最も時間をかけました。この曲の良さを引き出せないかと、聴かせるパートとそうでないパートの音量バランスを工夫しました。4パートの爽快な掛け合いの面白さで聴かせる曲ですね。精いっぱい頑張ったのですが、どうでしょうか。

*-----
「お猪の子守唄」の原曲がYoutubeなどで全く見つかりません。謎の民謡です。
ただ、吉田藩で起きた農民一揆をまとめたのが武左衛門だということはわかりました。
一揆は成功するのですが、後日約束を違えた吉田藩に捕らえられ処刑されてしまいます。
武左衛門を弔うのも禁止された中で、人々は（亥の子歌～いのこうた～の）替え歌で伝承してきたらしいです。

「じゅんのつぶやき」というBlogの、2013年5月18日の記事のコメントの中に、この曲の原曲かもしれない歌詞がありましたので転記させていただきます。

＜亥の子歌（宇和島市高光）＞
----------------------------------------
　一つ　非道のお裁きあれば
　二つ　ふせ火が下から起きる
　三つ　三間から騒動が起きた
　四つ　吉田を恨みに思う
　五つ　命にかけあう騒動
　六つ　村の武左衛門さまが
　七つ　何にも我身につけて
　八つ　八幡河原に揃う
　ここで九つ　紺屋の瀬戸で
　十と　武左衛門首斬られ給う

今回使用した昭和37年発行・40年第二刷のカワイ出版「多田武彦 男声合唱組曲集」の歌詞も転載します。（かけ声省略）
----------------------------------------
　一つ檜をお裁きなされ
　二つ不思議を下から願う
　三つ三間から騒動が起きて
　四つ吉田をうらみに思う
　五つ命に覚悟をなされ
　六つ無残や武左衛門さまは
　七つ何にもわが身にうけて
　八はた八幡河原にそろう
　ここで九つ紺屋のせどで
　十と武左衛門腹切りたもう

videos.title: 東京マルイ ハイキャパ5.1ガバメントモデル 蓄光BB弾 宅内10m試射 / Luminous BB shot, Tokyo Marui HI-CAPA 5.1 Government Model

localized.title: 東京マルイ ハイキャパ5.1ガバメントモデル 蓄光BB弾 宅内10m試射 / Luminous BB shot, Tokyo Marui HI-CAPA 5.1 Government Model
localized.description:
こんにちは トイガン初心者のお座敷シューターです。
東京マルイ ハイキャパ5.1 ガバメントモデルにトレーサー XCORTECH XT301 Mk2 を装着し、10mの距離で0.2gの蓄光BB弾を撃ってみました。
それだけの動画ですが よければご笑覧ください。

ハイキャパのアウターバレルを 11mm正ネジのDCI製品に交換して、トレーサーを装着しています。 (2024/5/25 14mm→11mmに修正)
狭い家で ふだんのお座敷シューティングでは10mも確保できないのですが、いちど10mで撃ってみたいと思い、家族の留守を狙って、家の端から端まで使って、なんとか10mを確保して撃つことができました。

BGM：BGMer(フリー素材)
・334:カクテルレシピ

Hi, I'm a toy gun beginner and an indoor-only shooter. This time I tried to shoot tracer BB bullets in 10 meters using Tokyo-Marui HI-CAPA 5.1 Government Model equipped with XCORTECH XT301 Mk2 Tracer.
Simply that's all for this movie. I would be glad if you sit back and enjoy watching.

To attach tracer, I replaced the original outer barrel of HI-CAPA 5.1 with a DCI optional barrel which has 14mm screw thread.
I can't hold 10 meter space for my usual in-room shooting, but I began to wish to shoot at 10 meter just once. So I used end to end of my small house and managed to hold 10 meters, and was able to shoot as I wished!

videos.title: 東京マルイ マイクロプロサイト→ハイキャパ5.1+DCIドクターサイトマウント 取り付け手順

localized.title: 東京マルイ マイクロプロサイト→ハイキャパ5.1+DCIドクターサイトマウント 取り付け手順
localized.description:
◆参考動画 / Reference Movies

(1)なんでもアートチャンネル
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=km4Hggj95ig&t=310
リアサイトの取り外し：5分10秒あたり

(2)Laylax
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vm9aMUaA8gU&t=402
リアサイトの取り外し：6分42秒あたり

(3)マック堺
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=safoSM30TaQ&t=244
リアサイトの取り外し：4分04秒あたり

(4)Laylax
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D0ZALDICEq8&t=390
シリンダーユニットの戻し：6分30秒～9分30秒あたり
－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－

トイガン初心者のお座敷シューターです。
今回、東京マルイ・ハイキャパ5.1ガバメントモデルに、DCI・ドクターサイトマウント・ハイキャパ用を台座にして、東京マルイ・マイクロプロサイトを取り付けました。
その手順を簡単にご説明します。

じつは、取付け手順書が付いていると思ってマウントを購入したのですが、付いておらず、説明動画などもないため、DCIに問い合せたところ、上記(1)の動画の前半を参考にしてリアサイトを外して付け換えてください、というガイドでした。

それで何とか取付けできましたが、少し迷う部分もあったので、同じような人の参考になればと、この動画を作りました。

Narration：Amazon Polly - Takumi
BGM：BGMer(フリー素材)
・071:午後の欅道

Hi, I'm a beginner and indoor-only toy-gun shooter.
Here's a brief instruction of attaching 'Tokyo Marui Micro Pro Sight' to 'Tokyo Marui Hi-Capa 5.1 Government Model' using 'DCI Doctor Sight Mount for Hi-Capa'

Actually, I purchased DCI mount assuming it comes with procedure manual, but it didn't. I couldn't find things like instruction movies either.
So I made an inquiry to DCI, and the answer was "detach the rear sight referring to the first half of the movie (1) above, and then attach the mount." I managed to attach the sight according to that, but also I found some confusing points.
I created this movie to be a small reference for someone in the same situation as me.
Sorry, the narrations and captions are in Japanese only.

localized.description:
「夢をかなえてドラえもん」は、アニメ「ドラえもん」のオープニング主題歌として2007年5月から約12年に渡って使用された曲。歌唱は女性シンガー mao で、リリースは同年7月。
2010年に作ったアカペラアレンジの細部に手を入れて、今回改めてアップしました。
"Yume wo Kanaete Doraemon" ("Make My Dreams Come True, Doraemon") is an OP theme song of the Doraemon anime series which had been used for about 12 long years since May, 2007. It was sung by Mao, a female Japanese singer, and was released in July, 2007.
This time I reworked details of this acappella arrangement, which was originally done in 2010, and newly posted here.

『ミックスナッツ』は、2022年4月にリリースされた、Official髭男dismの楽曲。同月放送開始のアニメ『SPY×FAMILY』第1期のオープニングテーマとして制作された。カオスなイントロ、「ビッグバンド＋モダンジャズ＋フュージョン」風の独特なテイスト、アーニャの好物であるピーナツに着想を得た軽妙洒脱な歌詞などが味わい深い傑作です。
"Mixed Nuts" is a song by Official HIGE DANdism released in Apr. 2022, It was written as the opening theme song of anime "SPY x FAMILY" season 1. This song has a chaotic introduction, unique taste like "big band + modern jazz + fusion", lyrics with full of wit and implications in the motif of "peanuts" which is Anya's favorite food, and those made the song a masterpiece.

「永遠にともに」（とわにともに）は、男性デュオ「コブクロ」が10枚目のシングルに収録し2004年にリリースした曲。シングルはオリコン週間チャート登場回数99回とコブクロ最大のロングヒットとなり、曲はウェディングソングの定番となっています。2009年に制作したアカペラアレンジを改訂しました。
"Towani Tomoni" ("Forever Together") is a song by Kobukuro, a Japanese male vocal duo, released with their 10th single in 2004. It became their longest hit appearing in Oricon weekly single chart 99 times, and the tune is now one of standard songs for wedding. This acappella arrangement is the rework of the original one produced in 2009.

videos.title: 世界に一つだけの花 (SMAP) / Sekai ni Hitotsu Dake no Hana - ボカロアカペラ / Vocaloid acappella (初音ミク+Kaito)

localized.title: 世界に一つだけの花 (SMAP) / Sekai ni Hitotsu Dake no Hana - ボカロアカペラ / Vocaloid acappella (初音ミク+Kaito)
localized.description:
「世界に一つだけの花」は、ジャニーズ事務所所属グループ「SMAP」がアルバムの1曲として2002年7月にリリースした曲。その後2003年3月に同グループ35枚目のシングルとして発売され、同年度のオリコンチャート1位となりました。また同チャート歴代累計3位、現在までにトリプルミリオン(300万枚)達成、各種ランキングでの最高位など、数々の称号を獲得しており、J-Popsの歴史に名を残す名曲となっています。2005年に作ったアカペラアレンジの細部に手を入れて、今回改めてアップしました。
"Sekai ni Hitotsu Dake no Hana" ("The One and Only Flower in the World") is a song by SMAP, a boys vocal group from "Johnny's Entertainment", which was released as one tune in their album in Jul., 2002. It was reissued as a single in Mar., 2003, and won the 1st place of the Oricon 2003 Yearly singles chart. Also it has been honored with many titles such as the third best-selling single in Japan in Oricon history, triple million total sales as of now, and top rank of various music awards in Japan. We can say the song is a masterpiece that made an imprint in J-Pops history. This time I reworked details of this acappella arrangement, which was originally done in 2005, and newly posted.

videos.title: やさしさに包まれたなら "Yasashisa ni Tsutsumareta nara" 荒井由実 - ボーカロイドアカペラ / Vocaloid acappella (初音ミク+Kaito)

localized.title: やさしさに包まれたなら "Yasashisa ni Tsutsumareta nara" 荒井由実 - ボーカロイドアカペラ / Vocaloid acappella (初音ミク+Kaito)
localized.description:
「やさしさに包まれたなら」は、1974年4月にリリースされた荒井由実（現：松任谷由実）の楽曲。アルバムバージョンを元にアカペラアレンジしました。スタジオジブリのアニメ映画「魔女の宅急便」(1989年)のエンディングテーマとしても知られています。
"Yasashisa ni Tsutsumareta nara" ("Wrapped in Kindness"), is a Japanese pop tune by Yumi Arai (currently Yumi Matsutoya) released in Apr., 1974. This acappella arrangement is based on its album version. This song is also known as the ending theme song of Hayao Miyazaki's anime film "Kiki's Delivery Service" ("Majo no Takkyuubin")(1989).

videos.title: 君をのせて "Carrying You" (Kimi o Nosete) from 天空の城ラピュタ - ボーカロイドアカペラ / Vocaloid acappella (初音ミク+Kaito)

localized.title: 君をのせて "Carrying You" (Kimi o Nosete) from 天空の城ラピュタ - ボーカロイドアカペラ / Vocaloid acappella (初音ミク+Kaito)
localized.description:
『君をのせて』は1986年に公開されたスタジオジブリ制作・宮崎駿監督のアニメ映画「天空の城ラピュタ」のエンディング主題歌として使われた、井上あずみの曲。同アニメはいまや伝説とも言える人気作品であり、その人気とあいまってこの曲も日本ではキッズソングのスタンダードとなっている。
"Carrying You" (in Japanese, "Kimi o Nosete") is the song performed by Azumi Inoue and used as the ending theme song of "Castle in the Sky" (天空の城ラピュタ, Tenkuu no Shiro Rapyuta), a 1986 Japanese anime film written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki. The film has now become a legendary masterpiece and widely popular over the world, and the song is now also a standard tune for kids in Japan.

videos.title: 勇気100% (光GENJI) Full / Yuuki Hyaku-percent - ボカロアカペラ / Vocaloid acappella (初音ミク+Kaito)

localized.title: 勇気100% (光GENJI) Full / Yuuki Hyaku-percent - ボカロアカペラ / Vocaloid acappella (初音ミク+Kaito)
localized.description:
『勇気100%』は、ジャニーズ事務所所属グループ「光GENJI」が21枚目のシングルとして1993年5月にリリースした曲で、同年4月スタートのテレビアニメ『忍たま乱太郎』のオープニング(OP)テーマに使用された。同アニメは以来現在まで30年近くに渡って放送されている長寿番組であり、『勇気100%』も同じジャニーズ事務所アーティストによって7回カバーされながら、同アニメのOP曲として使われ続けている。このことから日本では大人から子供まで広く親しまれている、J-Popsのレジェンドとも言える曲となっている。
"Yuuki Hyaku-percent(100%)" is the 21st single by Hikaru Genji, a boys vocal group from "Johnny's Entertainment", released in May, 1993. It was used as the opening theme song of the anime series "Nintama Rantaro" which started in Apr. in that year. The anime is a long-running program that keeps being on the air up until now, and this song has been also used as OP theme all the time, covered by different Johnny's artists seven times. It may be said that the song has become a "legend" J-Pops song that is widely popular among adults and kids in Japan.

videos.title: OUR LIVES 崎谷健次郎 by Kenjiro Sakiya - ボカロアカペラ / Vocaloid acappella（初音ミク+Kaito）歌詞付き w/ English

localized.title: OUR LIVES 崎谷健次郎 by Kenjiro Sakiya - ボカロアカペラ / Vocaloid acappella（初音ミク+Kaito）歌詞付き w/ English
localized.description:
"OUR LIVES" is the song written and sung by Kenjiro Sakiya, released in 1993 as the last tune of his album "HOLIDAYS" that includes 12 songs.It was in 2005 when I just happened to encounter this song and arranged it in acappella style. This time, I decided to refine the arrangement and post it. This is a very minor tune which didn't have big hit, but it is a good song filled with love and consideration. I remember I shed tears listening to this song in 2011 after the earthquake hit Japan...
OUR LIVES は1993年にリリースされた、12曲から成る崎谷健次郎のアルバム「HOLIDAYS」の最後の曲。私は2005年に偶然この曲に出会ってアカペラにアレンジしたことがあり、今回アレンジをし直してアップすることにしました。マイナー曲ですが、愛と思いやりにあふれた良曲です。2011年の大震災のとき、この曲を聞きながら涙したことを思い出します。

videos.title: Saint-Saëns Symphony #3 "Organ" 2nd mv later part Vocaloid acappella サン=サーンス オルガン交響曲2楽章後半-初音ミク+Kaito

localized.title: Saint-Saëns Symphony #3 "Organ" 2nd mv later part Vocaloid acappella サン=サーンス オルガン交響曲2楽章後半-初音ミク+Kaito
localized.description:
Saint-Saëns's Symphony No.3 is my best favorite classical orchestra music. Especially, the brilliance and magnificence of the later part of the 2nd movement is fabulous. At some time in the past, I started to vaguely consider arranging this music into acappella style, and now it came true unexpectedly earlier than I imagined.
One big driving power for me was an orchestra score of this symphony in handy size, which I got several years ago by some freak coincidence. This score gave me a lot of information. That is not just how I reproduce the famous melodies onto my score, but also many backing passages that I didn't notice listening to recorded orchestra sound without the score. It was a great joy for me to pursue note to note and to discover how Saint-Saëns elaborated this work to be a masterpiece.

サン=サーンスの交響曲第3番は、私が最も好きなクラシックのオーケストラ作品。特に第2楽章後半の壮麗さ、豪華さはすばらしい。いつの頃からか、この曲をアカペラ形式にアレンジしてみたいと思い始めたのですが、意外と早く実現しました。
今回の編曲の大きな推進力になったのが、何年か前にひょんなことで入手した、この曲のハンディサイズのオーケストラスコア本。このスコアからは、単に有名なメロディを再現するための情報だけでなく、スコアなしで曲を聴いていたときには気づかなかった、主旋律の裏で流れている数多くの副旋律があることを知ることができました。1つ1つ音符を追っていくことで、サン=サーンスがこの大曲を精緻に作り上げていった過程を発見できたのは、大きな喜びでした。

The objective of the game is simple. Shoot down all the enemy's battleplanes with your machine gun. It is good point that one round of the game takes only a few minutes.
You will face a difficulty to clear a stage at a certain level of the game, but do not give up. You can earn money using 'survival' stages to buy bullets and to enforce your gun, and get enough power for clearing the sky against deluging enemies.
I cleared all 'Campaign' stages two times and now got the gun power maximum. With this empowered gun, you can shoot down any enemy with normal bullets at earlier stages. This is a sample of that.

localized.title: 風のノー・リプライ "Kazeno No Reply" Full - ボーカロイドアカペラ / Vocaloid acappella（初音ミク+Kaito）
localized.description:
『風のノー・リプライ』は、1984年7月にリリースされた鮎川麻弥のデビュー曲で、テレビアニメ『重戦機エルガイム』の後期オープニングテーマ。作曲は、2020年10月に死去した日本歌謡界の巨匠、筒美京平。40年近く経つ今も輝きを失わない名曲です。
"Kazeno No Reply" is the debut song of Japanese singer Mami Ayukawa, which was released in Jul., 1984. It is also the opening theme song of the later part of anime "Heavy Metal L-Gaim". This song was composed by late Kyohei Tsutsumi, who was a great master in Japanese popular music scene and died in Oct., 2020. It is still a shining masterpiece after nearly 40 years from its release.

localized.title: Imperfect (インパーフェクト) Full - ボカロアカペラ / Vocaloid acappella（初音ミク+Kaito）
localized.description:
『インパーフェクト』は、2021年4月21日にリリースされたオーイシマサヨシの楽曲で、同時期に放送開始されたテレビアニメ『SSSS.DYNAZENON』のオープニングテーマ。彼の作風である半音進行を多用したドラマティックなコード展開や和声豊かでストレートなメロディはこの曲においても健在。感動し感化されて、アレンジにつながりました。
"Imperfect" is a song by Japanese pops and anime singer Masayoshi Oishi, which was released in Apr., 2021. It is also the opening theme song of the anime "SSSS.DYNAZENON" which went on air in Japan around the same time. His music style -- dramatic chord progression brought by heavy use of chromatic motion, harmonious and straightforward melody -- is also alive in this tune. It touched, inspired and lead me to this arrangement.

localized.description:
久しぶりのアカペラ制作は、「スーパー戦隊シリーズ」シリーズ45作記念作、「機界戦隊ゼンカイジャー」主題歌。今回はフルバージョンです。大変よい歌で創作意欲が湧き、GWは人生を考える時間にするはずだったのが、なぜか気づいたらこれを作っていました。ゼンカイダンスの動画もたくさんアップされていて楽しいですね。
It's been a long time since my last post. This is the opening theme of "Kikai Sentai Zenkaiger", the 45th memorial production of Super Sentai Series, and this time I made it full-length. This fabulous song stimulated my creative mind, and I strangely found myself completed this work while I was supposed to spend my Golden Week to ponder on my life... Also it is fun to see many movies of "Zenkai Dance" posted.

localized.description:
Butterfly is a Japanese pop song released in 2009 and one of Kaela Kimura's biggest hits that got the iTunes 2010 No.1 hit prize in Japan. Butterfly は2009年リリースの木村カエラのヒット曲で、2010年のiTunesにおいてDL数年間第1位を獲得した。木村自身が親友の結婚式のために作詞しており、美しい花嫁を蝶に、花婿を蝶が止まる花になぞらえている。

localized.description:

"Sehnsucht nach dem Fruehlinge" (Yearning for Spring) KV596

Composition: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
Arrangement: Gnagre
Song       : Hatsune Miku (Vocaloid 2)


花霧さん、猫柳ゆねさんの美麗なイラストを使用させていただきました。
素敵な絵を公開してくださってありがとうございます！


モーツァルト作曲　歌曲　K.596「春への憧れ」

和訳文と英訳文は、ドイツ語文の私なりの意訳ですので
恐縮ながら誤りを含んでいるかもしれません。

第9節の歌詞は所有する楽譜に記載されたものを用いました。
所有する2枚のCDはこれとは異なる方の（たぶん正しい？）歌詞なので
これは珍演奏になっているかもしれませんが
そうでなくとも初音ミクを使う時点で珍演奏なので敢えて。

ピアノはGPO4、歌は初音ミクを使用。
べた打ち直後の絶望感は半端ないものでした。
楽しめる範囲は私にはここまでが限界。
無声音ももちろんながら、ウムラウト（オームラウト）を
もう少し近い音声で発音させたいものですー。



***** original text *****

Komm, lieber Mai, und mache 
Die Bäume wieder grün,
Und laß mir an dem Bache 
Die kleinen Veilchen blüh'n!

Wie möcht' ich doch so gerne 
Ein Veilchen wieder she'n!
Ach, lieber Mai, wie gerne 
Einmal spazieren geh'n!

(Verses 3-8 abbreviated)

Ach, wenn's doch erst gelinder
Und grüner draußen wär'!
Komm, lieber Mai, wir Kinder,
Wir bitten gar zu sehr!

O komm und bring' vor allen
Uns viele Veilchen mit!
Bring' auch viel Nachtigallen
Und schöne Kuckucks mit!
